rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation aggressiveness upward while keeping the runtime-sensitive core of this program (mandel/fbench-style FP loops) protected from the costliest transforms: BCF and FLA keep RuntimeCost weights low (~0.35-0.4) so they are applied mainly to cold or control-flow-favoring functions rather than hot numeric kernels, while SUB gets a high SecurityGain (0.95) since instruction substitution is cheap and effective on arithmetic-heavy code, and IBR/ICALL/IGV get raised Security and Diversity weights to add inter-block randomization, indirect call indirection, and global-variable wiring that broaden structural diversity for reverse engineers. SPLIT stays moderate with high CorrectnessRisk tolerance since round 1 showed no ICE or miscompilation, giving headroom to split basic blocks more freely; all CorrectnessRisk weights remain high (0.7-0.9) to preserve the verified correctness from round 1, and no pass is disabled because the reference binary is tiny (1193 text bytes, 5 functions) and can absorb the size growth of full-coverage FLA/BCF/SPLIT without approaching overhead limits.
